answer: New identities start on a capacity ladder: two paid jobs in the first week, and the limit rises only after ten jobs are done cleanly, so reaching twenty jobs a week takes fifty verified jobs per identity. An attacker with 1,000 fakes must complete 50,000 clean jobs first, about 3 dollars of labor each, roughly 150,000 dollars before operating at scale. The ladder covers all work, from labeling a juniper specimen, to grading nectar samples, to checking an anchor chain. It works like a sailor proving himself on short trips before a long voyage.
